module_title: Advanced Articles - State Definition, Judicial Review, and Exceptions
introduction: This advanced level explores the foundational definitions of the State and Judicial Review, specific protections for convicts and minorities, and the complex relationship between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.

core_concepts.title: Definition of State (Article 12)
core_concepts.description: Defines 'the State' for the purpose of Part III. It includes the Govt and Parliament of India, Govt and Legislature of states, all local authorities (Panchayats, municipalities), and statutory/non-statutory bodies like LIC, ONGC, etc.

core_concepts.title: Judicial Review (Article 13)
core_concepts.description: Declares that all laws that are inconsistent with or in derogation of any of the fundamental rights shall be void. This implicitly grants the power of 'Judicial Review' to the Supreme Court and High Courts.

core_concepts.title: Protection in Conviction (Article 20)
core_concepts.description: Provides three critical protections: 1. No ex-post-facto law (cannot be punished for a past act that wasn't a crime then). 2. No double jeopardy (cannot be punished twice for the same offense). 3. No self-incrimination (cannot be forced to be a witness against oneself).

core_concepts.title: Preventive Detention (Article 22)
core_concepts.description: Grants protection to persons who are arrested or detained. However, it also validates 'Preventive Detention' (detaining someone before they commit a crime), setting a maximum initial period of 3 months without an advisory board's approval.

core_concepts.title: Minority Rights (Art 29 & 30)
core_concepts.description: Art 29: Protection of interests of minorities (right to conserve language, script, or culture). Art 30: Right of minorities (religious and linguistic ONLY) to establish and administer educational institutions.

core_concepts.title: The Exception Article (Article 31C)
core_concepts.description: Added by the 25th Amendment. It states that if a law is made to implement the socialist DPSPs under Art 39(b) or 39(c), it cannot be declared void just because it violates Art 14 (Equality) or Art 19 (Freedoms).

important_entities.name: Articles 20 and 21
important_entities.significance: Under the 44th Amendment Act, the rights guaranteed by Articles 20 and 21 CANNOT be suspended even during a National Emergency.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A very common UPSC trap statement: 'The Constitution defines the term minority.' FALSE. The Constitution uses the term (based on religion or language) in Articles 29 and 30 but nowhere does it define the word 'minority'.

Article 13(4) states that nothing in Art 13 applies to a constitutional amendment made under Art 368. However, the Kesavananda Bharati case ruled that even constitutional amendments can be struck down if they violate the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: No Ex-post-facto, No Double jeopardy, No Self-incrimination.

exam_strategy_tips: In Assertion-Reasoning questions, deeply understand how Article 31C acts as a shield for Article 39(b) and 39(c) against Articles 14 and 19.
Pay attention to the exact grounds of discrimination in Art 15 (Religion, Race, Caste, Sex, Place of birth) — 'Descent' and 'Residence' are added in Art 16 but absent in Art 15.
